title: Planner - Projects plan file
description: A project plan file, as Export writes it and Import reads it (format "project-plan", version 1). This schema says what a JSON Schema can say. Import also checks what it cannot: a day must be a real day from 1900 to 2200 (2026-02-30 and 2300-01-01 match the pattern but are refused); work's end is not before its start; every `parent` and `waitsOn` names an `id` in the file, no entry is part of itself, `parent` is a milestone, `waitsOn` is a milestone or work, and nothing waits on itself in a loop; each `id` is used once; when the plan's "Dates are needed" setting is on, a milestone needs a `start` and work a `start` and an `end`; text lengths count after trimming. Use the Check file entry in the Export and import menu for those. A file for Update by id has entries that carry only an `id` and `fields`, `start`, `end`, `owners` or `rank` (the `updateEntry` definition).
$comment: The format is written out in FORMAT.md beside this file. Fields that are not listed are ignored by Import, so additionalProperties is left open.

boards.description: The plan's board, as Export writes it. Optional; at most one for now.

fields.description: The plan's fields (Area, Phase and the like), as Export writes them. Optional; at most 8. A file's fields are added to the plan's by id.

day.description: YYYY-MM-DD, a real day from 1900 to 2200 (checked by Import, not by this pattern). Empty or null means no day.

columnId.description: A column id: lower case letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter.

done.description: true: work in this column counts as done.

color.description: The column's colour, a lower case #rrggbb, drawn as a dot and a light wash on its heading. Optional.

board.description: Needs at least one column that counts as done and one that does not, and each column id once (checked by Import, not by this schema).

value.description: In the size field: what the choice is worth (points, or a T-shirt size's number).

size.description: true: this is the plan's size field, whose choices' values are what the work is sized at. A plan has one.

field.description: A field: a short list of choices. Each id is used once in its list and at most one field has `size` (checked by Import, not by this schema).

fields.description: Work only: its choice in each field, { fieldId: choiceId }. The field and choice must be in the plan or in the file's `fields`.

rank.description: The order inside a board column.

updateEntry.description: An entry of a file for Update by id (an entry with no `kind`): the id of an entry in the plan and only what the space owns. Import refuses one that also names a title, a column or anything else the space does not own; a schema cannot say that.

id.description: 1 to 64 letters, digits, dashes or underscores; used once in the file. Needed only when another entry names this one.

title.description: Up to 120 characters, not only spaces.

parent.description: The id of a milestone in the file.

waitsOn.description: Ids of milestones or work in the file; at most 50.

owners.description: People's keys; leave out unless the file came from this environment.

tags.description: Tag ids from the plan's Tags setting.

column.description: Work only: the id of its column on the board. Work whose column the board does not have reads as the first done column if it is done, else the first column that does not count as done.

rank.description: The order inside a board column, as Export writes it. Leave it out when you write a file.

doneOn.description: Work only: the day it became done, as Export writes it. Kept only while the work is done. Leave it out when you write a file.

fields.description: Work only: its choice in each field, { fieldId: choiceId }. The field and choice must be in the plan or in the file's `fields`.

source.description: Where pulled work came from, as Export writes it (a pull from GitHub). Leave it out when you write a file.

then.$comment: A note has no days, no waitsOn and no done: Import ignores them.
A milestone has one day, start; an end is ignored. Import needs start when the plan needs dates.
Work has a start and an end, end not before start. Import needs both when the plan needs dates; with one, it takes it for both.
